newsitem.title: USA: Mexican official's drug money case opens in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Mexican official's drug money case opens in Texas.

text.p: Former Mexican Deputy Attorney General Mario Ruiz Massieu is set to appear in U.S. District Court in Houston on Monday to face allegations he stashed millions of dollars in payments from drug traffickers in a Texas bank.

While working as Mexico's top drug-fighter in the early 1990s, Ruiz Massieu allegedly received more than $9 million in drug proceeds in return for protecting traffickers and the massive shipments of cocaine they smuggled across the U.S.-Mexico border, prosecutors said.

Ruiz Massieu contested the government's right to seize the money in the civil forfeiture case, and in court documents said his Texas bank account held part of a family fortune made in real estate and business moved to the United States for safekeeping in the event of political or economic turmoil in Mexico.

"We had spoken about the convenience of taking most of our family's money out (of Mexico) by virtue of the fact that a guerrilla war had started in Mexico, and a series of economic and political problems was foreseen in the country," Ruiz Massieu said in a court filing.

The Ruiz Massieu case will be played out against the backdrop of increasing tensions on both sides of the border following President Bill Clinton's recent decision to recertify Mexico as a U.S. ally in the war on drugs.

A push in Congress to block the recertification drew sharp protests last week from leaders of Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party, or PRI, which said it was an attempt to destabilise the country.

Prosecutors plan to build their case against Ruiz Massieu largely on testimony of two convicted traffickers now cooperating with investigators, along with bank records detailing 26 deposits made into the Texas Commerce Bank account between December 1993 and February 1995, according to court filings.

One of the informants, identified in court filings as "Ms. Y", is believed to be Magdalena Ruiz Pelayo, a convicted drug trafficker who once worked as private secretary of Raul Salinas Lozano, the father of former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari and father-in-law of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, Mario Ruiz Massieu's brother.

According to court documents leaked to the Mexican weekly news magazine Proceso, Ruiz Pelayo said she was present when bribes were delivered to both Ruiz Massieu brothers, Mario and Jose Francisco, the number two official in the PRI, who was assassinated in September 1994.

Ruiz Massieu told prosecutors he opened the Texas bank account with an initial $40,000 deposit, and a courier made later deposits consisting of hundreds of thousands of dollars in cash bound with rubberbands or wrapped in cellophane and stuffed into travel bags.
Ruiz Massieu fled Mexico in 1995 in the face of narcotics-related corruption charges, and has remained in New Jersey after a federal court there rejected Mexico's extradition request.

The case will be tried in the same Houston courthouse where Mexican drug kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego was sentenced to 11 consecutive life terms earlier this year. Federal investigators said it would not mark the end of high-profile cases brought against allegedly corrupt senior Mexican officials.
"There will be a lot more of these kinds of trials coming up. You're going to see some interesting indictments this year," a senior U.S. drug official said.
